claims.text: A review is an informed judgement of a work, product, event or place, for readers deciding whether to try it.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The sections of a review are the introduction, the account of what is reviewed, the evaluation, and the verdict — and the balance leans evaluation: the reader can see the thing; they cannot see the judgement.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Planning a review means fixing the context, what the thing is, the criteria it will be judged by, the evidence for each, and the verdict — in that order, because criteria chosen after the evidence are criteria the evidence chose.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Reviewing is not recounting: a review judges, and a piece that tells the day’s events in order without weighing them has written an itinerary, not a judgement.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Recounting the experience in the order it happened, instead of judging it, is the review’s commonest failure: the reader deciding whether to come wants the verdict, not the timetable.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Spending the words on minor or side details — the journey there, the snacks, the parking — starves the evaluation the reader came for: the detail belongs to the review only when it carries evidence.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Criteria are the standards a review judges by, and they are chosen by the reviewer, stated in the review, and shared with the reader before the verdict is asked of them.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Evidentiary logic is the review’s spine: every judgement is followed by the evidence that supports it, so the reader can check the reasoning rather than borrow the verdict.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Listing features or activities without evaluating any of them is the review’s empty version: the reader is given the contents page and no verdict.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Judging whether a verdict is justified means checking the evidence given against the claim made: the strongest verdicts state their terms, show their workings, and are big enough to admit what fell short.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Evaluative lexis is the vocabulary of judgement — graded words that say how good, how bad, and in what way, rather than the general praise that could attach to anything.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Graded evaluative vocabulary runs from the adequate to the outstanding and from the disappointing to the dire, and the grade names the level: a review that only says "good" and "bad" has a scale with two rungs.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A balanced verdict is a weighed judgement that names the best and the worst and says which the reader should weight; a list of likes and dislikes is a tally, and a tally is not a judgement.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Offering personal likes and dislikes with no criteria and no critique is taste without an argument: the reader learns what the reviewer enjoyed and nothing about whether they would enjoy it.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The review/critical task is set as a review in every paper of the corpus — one of the three Section B categories, 600–900 words, twenty-five marks.
